label: GO after a2-S1-unrewarded; larger early in episode and after prior reward
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * np.clip(ep_trial,0,60) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (tv("action", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (tv("action", -2) == -9) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * belief_lo
explanation: Fires only at GO, and almost only when the previous trial was a2 -> rare S1, unrewarded (an additive previous-trial table gets 0.28). Magnitude within that case, all from observed quantities: about 0.9 at the start of the episode, falling about 0.019 per trial until it is near zero by trial ~50-60 (linear clip at 60 beats an exponential); +0.36 if the trial before was rewarded; -0.16 if the trial before was an a1 choice; +0.28 when the trial before is outside the window (window-start context); repeated a2-S1-u streaks decay it (absorbed by the reward(-2) term). Higher when the ideal-observer belief favours S2 (belief_lo weight -0.06; adds only ~0.004). Test R^2 beyond timing 0.584 (dev 0.603), well above the additive all-cues ceiling of 0.32 because of the interactions with the a2-S1-u gate. No model outputs used. The policy-decile reference alone was 0.09 versus 0.06 for belief, so leaving out value/policy appears to lose little; the earlier model-based score was not re-measured here.

issues: The score reproduces: test R^2 beyond timing is 0.584 with the claimed weights (0.708, -0.019/trial, +0.362, -0.159, +0.279, -0.063). The direction of each main claim holds when you drop terms on test: gate + ep_trial alone gives 0.525, adding reward(-2) gives 0.562, adding the action(-2) terms gives 0.580. Dropping the ep_trial term falls to 0.308, so the episode-position effect is real.

The trial-before reward effect is described as a flat additive '+0.36', but it is mostly multiplicative with episode position. Adding gate*reward(-2)*clip(ep_trial) alone raises test R^2 from 0.584 to 0.617. In a fully multiplicative form with decay D = clip(1 - ep_trial/65, 0, 1), the weights are gate*D 0.36 and gate*D*reward(-2) 1.11. So early in the episode a rewarded trial-2 roughly triples the response. It is the dominant modifier, not a side bump.

'Repeated a2-S1-u streaks fade it' is not backed by any term, and testing contradicts it. Adding gate*(trial-2 also a2 S1 u) gains 0.0000 on test (0.58398 vs 0.58397). In the multiplicative model its weight is +0.19, not negative. The apparent fade within streaks in the misses windows (1.45 -> 0.97 -> 0.50 -> 0.13) is better explained by the absence of a rewarded trial-2 plus the window-edge term.

The '+0.28 if the trial before falls outside the window' term is a data-window artifact, not a behavioural driver: the agent did see that trial. It should not be reported as a property of the feature. Related: GO steps on the window's first trial with an unseen previous trial (prev_reward = 0) fire strongly but are predicted at about 0.09 (misses windows: [-3 t7] actual 1.45 vs predicted 0.086, [-3 t5] 1.46 vs 0.086). A term for that case adds +0.012 on test.
The linear clip(ep_trial, 0, 60) decline is the wrong shape. A squared term adds +0.006 on test, and a multiplicative linear decay to zero at about trial 65 fits better: 0.654 vs 0.584.

The belief claim is fine but minor: belief_lo inside the gate has weight -0.05 to -0.06 and adds about 0.005. Nonlinear belief variants add at most 0.001. The choice about to be made (future) adds 0.0002, so 'staying confidently on a2' from the earlier firing-based label is not needed for magnitude.

Remaining misses are not concentrated in any phase x previous-trial cell (mean errors about ±0.02, and those come from the baseline spreading over GO steps that never fire). So no large error class remains beyond the functional-form problems above. The verdict is rejected because two stated claims (the streak fade and the additive window-edge effect) are unsupported or artifacts, and the reward effect is misdescribed.
